blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: There are no towels in room 15.
exercises.why: The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative: *Я пью молоко. — Я не пью молока. Я вижу реку. — Я не вижу реки.* The verb ждать takes no preposition. The object is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate: *Я жду жену. Я жду письма. The genitive case is used to denote an indefinite quantity of something: *Дайте воды, молока, хлеба.* Several masculine nouns may take the ending -у, -ю (instead of -а, -я) in the genitive case when a quantity is expressed: *Дайте, пожалуйста, супу, сахару, чаю. Хотите стакан чаю? — DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33.  ·  «The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative.» «Conversely, to say 'There isn't...', 'There aren't...', we use the word нет followed by the genitive case.» — DLI, Lesson 27; Wikibooks, «Genitive case».
exercises.context: The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative: *Я пью молоко. (DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33)
